title: chore(legal): NIW2-566 AGPL-3.0-only license text, commercial use in terms, trademark policy and CLA
body:
Linear: [NIW2-566](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-566/licensing-hygiene-agpl-30-only-commercial-use-in-terms-trademark)

A review of how Cap ([CapSoftware/Cap](https://github.com/CapSoftware/Cap)) makes money from an AGPL desktop app turned up four places where Kaipu's licensing was inconsistent or left a gap. This PR closes them. It changes no runtime behavior: two legal strings (en + es), one version constant, and documents.

1. **The license contradicted itself.** `LICENSE` opened with a header saying "version 3, or (at your option) any later version", while `package.json`, the README and CONTRIBUTING declare `AGPL-3.0-only`. Those are different licenses. `LICENSE` is now the unmodified text from gnu.org (sha256 `0d96a4ff…abcb0`), so GitHub can detect it (it shows "Other" today). The copyright line and the version-3-only notice move to the README's License section.
2. **The terms granted a "personal" license.** Cap uses "personal use" to mean non-commercial, so a company reading our terms could conclude it has to pay to use Kaipu at work. That contradicts the filesystem-first monetization ADR. The clause now says the app may be used for personal or commercial purposes without a paid plan. The legal version is bumped to 2026-10-30.
3. **`TRADEMARKS.md`.** The AGPL licenses the code, not the name. A distributed fork uses its own name and icon.
4. **`CLA.md`.** The owner wants outside contributions and full ownership. Contributors keep their copyright and grant Niway S.A.C. a broad license, including the right to relicense. Versions already published under the AGPL stay under the AGPL. Contributors sign by commenting on their first PR; there is no bot. CONTRIBUTING and the PR template point to it. This keeps the source-available fallback in `marketing/open-source.md` possible, which is exactly what Cap gave up by accepting contributions without a CLA.
5. **Docs drift.** `open-source.md` claimed that every `package.json` declares the license (4 of 19 do) and that the repository stays private (it has been public since 2026-10-05).

It also records the owner's decision on a **voluntary supporter license** as a 🔵 Proposed backlog page. It funds development and never gates use. The design work is tracked in [NIW2-567](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-567/supporter-license-voluntary-symbolic-payment-that-funds-development).

**The CLA and the trademark policy are project drafts, not reviewed by a lawyer.** They are added to the legal review already pending in `backlog/legal-documents.md`.

## What to review

1. **`CLA.md` §2 and §5: the relicensing grant and its single limit.** Decide whether "under any license terms Niway chooses, including proprietary terms" is what you want in exchange for contributions, and whether the "published AGPL versions stay AGPL" promise is enough to reassure contributors. Section 2 is the reason the file exists.
2. **`README.md` License section: the copyright holder.** It reads "Copyright (C) 2025-2026 Cristian Sotomayor, published by Niway S.A.C.", while the CLA and TRADEMARKS name Niway S.A.C. as the grantee and mark owner. Confirm who should hold the copyright. The old header said "Cristian Sotomayor on NIWAY".
3. **`packages/i18n/messages/es.json:1367` (Spanish prevails): the new license wording.** Check that "con fines personales o comerciales" plus "no requiere un plan de pago" says what you mean and does not promise anything about Cloud.
4. **`TRADEMARKS.md`, "What needs written permission".** Decide whether the bundle ID and update-channel line is the right scope for forks.

**Safe to skim:** `LICENSE` (verbatim gnu.org text), the docs changes, `legal-config.ts` (a date), and the PR template comment.

## Checks

- `oxfmt --check .`: all 1937 files formatted.
- `packages/i18n` tests: 22 passed (5 files), including `plan-copy.test`.
- `apps/web-hono` `route-messages.test.ts`: 20 passed.
- Pre-push `verify-local` (lint, format, builds, types): 24/24 tasks successful.
- Docs site build: not run locally. The sidebar slug `backlog/supporter-license` matches the new file.

## Manual verification

- [ ] GitHub shows "AGPL-3.0 license" in the repo sidebar after merge (detection runs on the default branch).
- [ ] `/legal/terms-and-conditions` shows the new license paragraph and "Updated October 30, 2026" in both languages.

## How to test it yourself

1. `bun run dev` in this checkout, open the web app and go to `/legal/terms-and-conditions`.
2. Under **Software and intellectual property** you should read "…for personal or commercial purposes. Using the desktop app for work, including inside a company, needs no paid plan." The header should say **Updated October 30, 2026 · Version 2026-10-30**.
3. Switch to Spanish: the same paragraph says "con fines personales o comerciales… no requiere un plan de pago".
4. For contrast, on `main` the paragraph starts "Niway grants you a personal, revocable…" with no mention of commercial use.
5. Open `CLA.md` and `TRADEMARKS.md` on the PR's **Files** tab and read the "In one minute" section of the CLA: it should match what you want contributors to agree to.
6. Docs: `bun run dev` in `apps/documentation`, then open **Backlog → Supporter license** and **Marketing → Open source under AGPL-3.0**.
